# @ic-reactor/react

> React hooks, reusable query/mutation objects and Internet Identity sign-in
> for Internet Computer canisters, on TanStack Query. Re-exports all of
> `@ic-reactor/core`.

Applies to `@ic-reactor/react` 3.13.0.

Read this file from `node_modules/@ic-reactor/react/llms.txt` when writing
code against the installed version. The complete guide for every package is
https://ic-reactor.b3pay.net/llms-full.txt, and behaviour changes are in
https://github.com/B3Pay/ic-reactor/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/react @icp-sdk/core @tanstack/react-query
pnpm add @icp-sdk/auth@^10 # optional: Internet Identity sign-in
```

Needs `@tanstack/react-query` 5.90.2 or later, React 18 or later and
TypeScript 5.7 or later. Import the runtime (`ClientManager`, `Reactor`,
`DisplayReactor`, errors, token helpers) from `@ic-reactor/react` as well; do
not add `@ic-reactor/core` beside it. `@icp-sdk/auth` v10 is recommended and
v8 still works; on npm, v8 needs
`{"overrides":{"@icp-sdk/auth":{"@icp-sdk/core":"$@icp-sdk/core"}}}` in
`package.json`. v7 and v9 are not supported.

## Setup and Usage

```tsx
// src/reactor.tsx
import { defineReactor, isCanisterError, skipToken } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { canisterId, idlFactory, type _SERVICE } from "./declarations/backend"

export const {
  reactor: backend,
  useActorQuery,
  useActorMutation,
  useAuth,
} = defineReactor<_SERVICE>({ name: "backend", idlFactory, canisterId })

export function Profile({ userId }: { userId?: string }) {
  const profile = useActorQuery({
    functionName: "get_profile",
    args: userId ? [userId] : skipToken, // no call until the id exists
  })
  const rename = useActorMutation({
    functionName: "update_profile",
    invalidateQueries: [{ functionName: "get_profile" }], // refetched first
    onCanisterError: (err) => console.warn("Refused:", err.code), // Err variant
  })

  if (!userId) return <p>Sign in first</p>
  if (profile.isPending) return <p>Loading…</p>
  if (profile.error) {
    const { error } = profile
    return <p>{isCanisterError(error) ? error.code : error.message}</p>
  }
  return (
    <button
      disabled={rename.isPending}
      onClick={() => rename.mutate([{ name: "Ada" }])}
    >
      {profile.data.name}: {profile.data.likes.toString()} likes
    </button>
  )
}
```

`defineReactor` builds the `QueryClient` (query retry `reactorRetry`), the
`ClientManager`, a `Reactor` with raw Candid values (`bigint`, `Principal`),
the six hooks of `createActorHooks`, and `useAuth`, `useAgentState`,
`useUserPrincipal`, `useIdentityAttributes`, `authentication`,
`identityAttributes`. `defineDisplayReactor` takes the same options and gives
display values instead (strings for `bigint` and `Principal`, hex for blobs,
`T | undefined` for `opt`, `{ _type: "A", A: value }` for a variant, and just
`{ _type: "A" }` for a case without a value). `canisterId` is required except
on a local replica whose `ic_env` cookie names it. `./declarations/backend`
stands for your canister's declarations: `idlFactory` from the generated
`.js`, `_SERVICE` from the `.d.ts` (with the CLI or the Vite plugin,
`src/declarations/<name>/declarations/<did>.js` and `.d.ts`, named after the
`.did` file), and `canisterId` your canister's id as text.

## When to Use What

| Need                                          | Use                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Client-only app, raw Candid values            | `defineReactor(...)` at module scope                                              |
| Client-only app, values for forms and display | `defineDisplayReactor(...)` at module scope                                       |
| A reactor you built yourself                  | `createActorHooks(reactor)`                                                       |
| Server-rendered app (Next.js, any SSR)        | `createReactorProvider(() => defineReactor(...))` in a `"use client"` module      |
| React Server Component, server action, route  | `ClientManager` + `Reactor` from this package, built in the request; `fetchQuery` |
| One call used in components and loaders       | `createQuery`, `createQueryFactory` (args later), `createMutation`                |
| Suspense                                      | `useActorSuspenseQuery`, `createSuspenseQuery`, `createSuspenseQueryFactory`      |
| Paginated reads                               | `useActorInfiniteQuery`, `createInfiniteQuery`, `createInfiniteQueryFactory`      |
| One hook for a query or update with `call()`  | `useActorMethod`                                                                  |
| Another canister with the same interface      | `reactor.forCanister(canisterId)`, or `callConfig: { canisterId }` for one query  |
| A second canister on the same sign-in         | `defineReactor({ ..., authentication: firstApp.authentication })`                 |
| Sign-in with a manual setup                   | `createAuthHooks(new AuthenticationManager({ clientManager }))`                   |
| Tests                                         | `installFakeReplica` + `createTestCanister` from `@ic-reactor/react/testing`      |

## Inside React vs Outside React

- In components and custom hooks: `useActorQuery`, `useActorMutation`,
  `useActorMethod`, `useAuth`, `.useQuery()`, `.useMutation()`,
  `.useSuspenseQuery()`, `.useInfiniteQuery()`.
- In loaders, actions, services, scripts and non-hook tests: query objects'
  `.fetch()`, `.prefetch()`, `.invalidate()`, `.getCacheData()`,
  `.setData()`, `.cancel()`, `.reset()`, `.optimisticUpdate()`; mutation
  objects' `.execute(args)`; and the reactor's `.fetchQuery()`,
  `.getQueryData()`, `.invalidateQueries()`, `.callMethod()`.
- `.fetch()` and `reactor.fetchQuery()` fetch again as the new principal when a
  sign-in or sign-out lands mid-fetch; they never reject with TanStack's
  `CancelledError`. `.prefetch()` fetches again the same way and never
  rejects, and a query method's `call()` / `refetch()` from `useActorMethod`
  resolve with the new principal's answer (`undefined` if that fetch fails).
  Wrap your own `queryClient.fetchQuery` or
  `fetchInfiniteQuery` of a canister query in
  `clientManager.fetchAcrossIdentitySwitch(() => ...)`.

```ts
import { createMutation, createQueryFactory } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { backend } from "./reactor"

export const getPost = createQueryFactory(backend, { functionName: "get_post" })
export const likePost = createMutation(backend, {
  functionName: "like_post",
  invalidateQueries: [getPost], // every cached post, whatever its args
})

// In a component: getPost([id]).useQuery(), likePost.useMutation()
// In a loader:    await getPost([id]).fetch()
// In an action:   await likePost.execute([id])
```

## Server Rendering

A reactor owns its `QueryClient` and query keys carry no caller principal, so
a module-scope reactor on a server is one cache shared by every request. In a
server-rendered app, build reactors per mounted provider:

```tsx
"use client"
import { createReactorProvider, defineReactor } from "@ic-reactor/react"
import { canisterId, idlFactory, type _SERVICE } from "./declarations/backend"

export const { ReactorProvider, useReactor } = createReactorProvider(() =>
  defineReactor<_SERVICE>({ name: "backend", idlFactory, canisterId })
)
// layout: <ReactorProvider>{children}</ReactorProvider>
// component: const { useActorQuery, useAuth } = useReactor()
```

- The factory runs once per mounted provider (once per request on a server).
  It may return a record (`useReactor("ledger")`) and query/mutation objects
  built inside it. `useReactor()` is typed as the factory's return: never write
  `as any` hook forwarders or a hand-rolled context provider.
- On unmount it disposes the `AuthenticationManager`s built for its value.
  When the value holds exactly one `QueryClient` (its reactors share one
  `ClientManager`), it renders a `QueryClientProvider` for it
  (`{ queryClientProvider: false }` to keep your own).
- Props other than `children` go to the factory, read once per mount; change
  the provider's `key` to rebuild. A provider mounted by a transition needs a
  `<Suspense>` boundary inside it around suspending components.
- A React Server Component, server action or route handler may import
  `Reactor`, `DisplayReactor`, `ClientManager` and the rest of the core runtime
  from `@ic-reactor/react`: its `react-server` export condition resolves to an
  entry without React. Hooks, `defineReactor`, `defineDisplayReactor`,
  `createActorHooks`, `createReactorProvider`, the query/mutation factories,
  `skipToken` and the auth classes are missing exports there.

## Queries

- `skipToken` in place of args waits without calling the canister:
  `args: owner ? [account] : skipToken` in `useActorQuery`,
  `getArgs: owner ? (page) => [...] : skipToken` in `useActorInfiniteQuery`,
  `getBalance(owner ? [account] : skipToken).useQuery()` with
  `createQueryFactory` (that skipped object has only `useQuery()`). The
  suspense hooks, `createQuery` and `createSuspenseQuery` do not take it.
- Paginated reads: `createInfiniteQuery` (or `useActorInfiniteQuery`) takes
  `functionName`, `initialPageParam`, `getNextPageParam` and
  `getArgs: (page) => [...] as const`. Keep `as const`: without it
  `createInfiniteQuery` infers an array rather than the argument tuple and
  rejects it.
- A `Result` is unwrapped: `data` is the `Ok` payload and an `Err` arrives as a
  `CanisterError` in `error`.
- Query hooks and objects take TanStack's options (`select`, `staleTime`,
  `enabled`, ...) and `callConfig` (`canisterId`, `agent`,
  `effectiveCanisterId`).
- Several tokens of one interface: `reactor.forCanister(canisterId)` returns a
  memoized sibling reactor on the same `ClientManager`. Build hooks on it with
  `useMemo(() => createActorHooks(ledger.forCanister(id)), [id])`.
- Types: `ReactorArgsOf<typeof reactor, "method">[0]`,
  `ReactorDataOf<typeof reactor, "method">`,
  `ReactorErrorOf<typeof reactor, "method">`.

## Mutations, Invalidation and Retries

- Call state-changing update methods only through `useActorMutation`,
  `useActorMethod` or `createMutation`. A query runs its method again on every
  refetch, and each run of an update executes on the canister.
- `invalidateQueries` takes query objects, query factories (every args
  instance) and `{ functionName, args? }` methods of the mutation's reactor,
  keyed at the canister the mutation was sent to. It is awaited before
  `onSuccess`. Every key starts with the canister id, so a hand-written
  `["get_posts"]` matches nothing.
- `onCanisterError` receives the `CanisterError` of an `Err` result
  (`err.code`, `err.err`); `onError` receives every error.
- Mutations retry nothing unless `retry` is set, on them or as the
  `QueryClient`'s `mutations.retry` default (which reaches `execute()` and
  `useActorMethod` update calls too). Use `retry: reactorUpdateRetry`, which
  retries only a `SysTransient` rejection, never a number.
- Optimistic UI: return `query.optimisticUpdate(updater)` from `onMutate`,
  call `update?.rollback()` in `onError`, and `invalidate()` in `onSettled`.
  When you need the `QueryClient`, use `reactor.queryClient`:
  `useQueryClient()` throws without a `QueryClientProvider`.

## Sign-In

- `useAuth()` gives `login`, `logout`, `isAuthenticated`,
  `isAuthenticating`, `principal`, `identity` and `error`. It reports
  `isAuthenticating: true` until the first session restore settles, and in
  every server render: check it before redirecting on `!isAuthenticated`.
- `createAuthHooks` takes an `AuthenticationManager`, never a `ClientManager`,
  and returns `useAuth`, `useAgentState` and `useUserPrincipal`.
  `useIdentityAttributes` comes from `createIdentityAttributeHooks`.
- Pass an identity-attribute nonce as a callback (`nonce: async () => ...`),
  not an awaited value, so the popup opens within the click.
- `authentication.dispose()` releases the auth client the manager built,
  without signing out.

## Testing

Run the real reactor and hooks against `installFakeReplica` and
`createTestCanister` from `@ic-reactor/react/testing`. Install the fake before
any `ClientManager` is built: for a module-scope `defineReactor`, at the top of
the test file, then `await import(...)` the components. Generated code is
module scope too: import `idlFactory` and `_SERVICE` from the canister's
`declarations/` folder, key the fake by the `canisterId` the generator wrote,
and `await import(...)` the entry after the fake. A handler returns
`{ Err: ... }` for a `CanisterError` and throws for a `CallError`. Reset a
shared reactor with `queryClient.clear()`, and test a signed-in user with
`clientManager.updateAgent(identity)`.

## Do Not

- Call hooks outside components and custom hooks, or create hooks with
  `createActorHooks` / `createAuthHooks` on every render.
- Put a state-changing update method in `useActorQuery`, `createQuery` or
  `createQueryFactory`.
- Give an update mutation a numeric `retry`; use `reactorUpdateRetry`.
- Hand-write query keys, or add the canister id to a `queryKey`.
- Write `args: [userId!]`, a placeholder account, or `as any` plus `enabled`;
  pass `skipToken`.
- Check `"Ok" in data`; the `Result` is already unwrapped.
- Use `Number(x) / 10 ** decimals`; use `formatTokenAmount` and
  `parseTokenAmount`.
- Retarget a shared reactor with `setCanisterId`; use `forCanister`.
- Write `defineReactor({ display: true })`; use `defineDisplayReactor`.
- Build reactors or managers at module scope in a server-rendered app, or
  import hooks into a server component.
- Stub a reactor with `as unknown as Reactor` in tests.
- Edit `index.generated.ts` or `index.factories.generated.ts`.
